bib.title: PEDAL: Enhancing Greedy Decoding with Large Language Models using Diverse Exemplars

question: Can diverse in-context exemplars with greedy decoding, aggregated by an LLM, beat plain greedy decoding in accuracy at lower output-token cost than Self-Consistency?
hypothesis: Greedy decoding over prompts with diverse exemplars, aggregated as in USC, gives better accuracy than greedy decoding and lower inference cost than SC-based methods.
contributions: PEDAL, a hybrid self-ensembling approach combining diverse-exemplar prompts and LLM-based aggregation
Experiments on SVAMP and ARC-Challenge showing higher accuracy than greedy and fewer output tokens than USC

method.summary: Build several ICL prompts by randomly sampling exemplars with different seeds, generate one greedy response per prompt, then have the same LLM pick the most consistent response (USC-style aggregation). Compared with greedy, USC, and a unified-diverse-exemplars prompt on SVAMP and ARC-Challenge using two 7-8B instruct models.
method.task: arithmetic word problems and multiple-choice science QA

inference.decoding: greedy for PEDAL candidates and baseline; USC uses SC sampling (settings not given)
inference.samples: 3 random seeds, mean +- std reported; USC 3 intermediate outputs; PEDAL 3 diverse prompts (2 and 4 in ablation)
inference.prompting: 3 exemplars per ICL prompt; exemplars randomly sampled per seed; USC uses CoT prompting

parameters.aggregation: same LLM, USC-style selection of most consistent response

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match (per conclusion); averaged over 3 seeds

metrics.name: Token count
metrics.definition: input and output tokens consumed by strategy

baselines: UDE (Unified Diverse Exemplars: all diverse exemplars in a single ICL prompt, greedy)
eval.protocol: 3 seeds, mean +- std; no significance test

results.claim: Number of prompts on SVAMP/Qwen2: accuracy 77.0 (2), 77.89 (3), 78.22 (4); no clear pattern on ARC.
Interpolated single-CoT output tokens vs PEDAL: PEDAL likely cheaper except possibly Qwen2 on SVAMP; authors call this preliminary.
results.setup: Interpolation from Tables 3 and 5, not measured

limits: Only two small datasets (300 and 345 items) chosen so exact match works; free-form generation is future work.
USC underperforms greedy on ARC with Llama3 (71.88 vs 76.52); authors leave this unexplained.
CoT comparison is a preliminary interpolation, not a run; PEDAL may cost more than CoT on SVAMP/Qwen2.
PEDAL uses more input tokens than USC in most settings; cost claim counts output tokens only.
Gains over greedy are small relative to seed std on some cells (ARC Qwen2 +0.39 vs std 0.47-0.55); no significance test.
Not stated: sampling temperature for USC, exemplar source, max tokens, prompt text, code release.
